narrative.overview: FinPal is a calm financial operations environment suspended between a PayPal-adjacent night sky and a precise control console. Deep blue-black canvases, frosted glass, restrained light blooms, and a translucent payment card give the product atmosphere without making money movement feel theatrical or opaque. The marketing surface persuades through one exact scroll story: a long, sticky first scene resolves into an evaluated-first second scene. The application surface tightens the same world into a glassy shell, dense evidence panels, explicit decision branches, and monospace operational labels. Expression belongs in the environment; financial state and action remain literal, scannable, and calm.
keyCharacteristics: Blue-black, full-bleed environments framed by large rounded containers.
Frost-white action surfaces and icy blue light used sparingly as operational emphasis.
Geist for clear hierarchy; Geist Mono for states, indices, paths, and machine-readable evidence.
Translucent panels, hairline borders, and ambient blur instead of heavy card chrome.
Explicit branches and diagrams for policy, architecture, and payment state.
Motion that is slow, spatial, and removable without loss of meaning.

rules.name: The Sparse Signal Rule
rules.body: Frost, amber, and coral are state-bearing colors, not decoration; the dark field must remain dominant.

rules.name: The Explicit Status Rule
rules.body: Never communicate a financial outcome by color alone. Pair every hue with a literal label such as AUTO_APPROVE, MANUAL_REVIEW, BLOCK, AUTHORIZED, or VOIDED.

rules.name: The Two-Register Rule
rules.body: Geist speaks to people; Geist Mono speaks for the system. Do not set general prose or large headings in mono.

rules.name: The Quiet Weight Rule
rules.body: Large type earns authority through scale and spacing, not bold weight; reserve 500–600 for compact controls and local emphasis.

rules.name: The Ambient-Not-Decorative Rule
rules.body: Blur and glow establish the night environment or clarify an active state; they never sit behind routine text merely for style.

rules.name: The Glass Needs an Edge Rule
rules.body: Every translucent control surface needs a hairline border so its boundary remains legible over gradients and orbs.

dos: Do preserve the blue-hour control-room atmosphere across both persuasion and operation surfaces.
Do use exact monospace labels for machine states, evidence thresholds, architecture, and audit language.
Do show payment branches explicitly, including capture versus void, and pair every status color with text.
Do frame major landing sections as large rounded environments with narrow outer gutters.
Do keep app panels translucent, bordered, and readable over the ambient orb.
Do honor keyboard focus, horizontal overflow, mobile stacking, and reduced-motion fallbacks.
donts: Don't imply live money movement; keep PayPal Sandbox or equivalent simulated-funds context visible where payment actions occur.
Don't turn frost, amber, or coral into decorative palette colors.
Don't replace explicit decision tables, state flows, or architecture layers with vague illustrations.
Don't use generic bright-blue SaaS gradients, solid white cards, or heavy drop shadows.
Don't put body copy in Geist Mono or make operational labels oversized.
Don't animate financial outcomes in a way that hides, delays, or changes their meaning.
